title: Capacity-bleed Handshake: graceful routing handshake from Dedicated -> Hosted with safety gates
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: When dedicated GPU pools are saturated or under maintenance we need a predictable, auditable, and tenant-safe way to route overflow traffic to hosted capacity. Existing spillover logic is reactive and can cause noisy neighbor effects, sudden latency spikes, and cost runway surprises for tenants. This ticket designs, implements and validates a 'capacity-bleed handshake'—a coordinated, rate-limited, multi-signal transition from Dedicated -> Hosted with automatic rollback and variant demotion safeguards.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Implement a handshake protocol that transitions a tenant's route to hosted gradually in N phases (probe, soft-bleed, full-bleed) with configurable time windows.
- Rate-limit token injection to hosted by tenant and region so hosted cost exposure is bounded per tenant.
- Honor tenant affinity and contractual reservations: never exceed tenant's dedicated reservation threshold unless explicitly allowed by override.
- Variant fallback policy: prefer quantized/cheaper model variants on hosted during bleed; offer configurable quality guardrails and automatic regression detection.
- Expose telemetry and dashboards for bleed events including tenant, from-region, to-region, phase, token-rate, latency and 95/99 P95/P99 deltas.
- Provide a runbook and run integration test harness and chaos tests.

Scope of work:
- API/config: add handshake policy object to routing config with phases, limits, and variant map.
- Orchestrator: implement state machine for probe -> soft-bleed -> full-bleed with timers and rollback triggers.
- Quota controller: tenant-level hosted burst budget and per-region throttles.
- Variant demotion service: map model variants for hosted backfill and compute expected quality delta.
- Observability: bleed event logs, SLO deltas, cost delta estimation.
- Safety: automatic rollback on latency degradation above thresholds or error-rate increases.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Capacity-Bleed+Handshake+Design
- API proto PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-orch/pull/412
- Spike notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcExampleSpikeNotes
- Initial dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/bleed-handshake/overview

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer a staged approach because abrupt failover causes client-visible latency cliffs; probe stage samples RPS to hosted at 1% to measure tail latency and model quality.
- Cost vs latency trade-off: soft-bleed uses quantized variants to reduce hosted cost but may reduce quality. We will expose a tuning knob per-tenant: cost-priority | latency-priority | quality-priority.
- Complexity: introducing a handshake state machine adds code paths in the orchestrator and requires strong testing. We mitigate by reusing existing routing circuit-breaker abstractions.
- Locking/resilience: orchestrator will persist handshake state in the routing-store with optimistic concurrency to avoid split-brain when multiple controllers reconcile.

Monitoring and metrics (initial list):
- bleed_event_total{phase,tenant,from_region,to_region} (counter)
- bleed_probe_error_rate{tenant} (gauge)
- bleed_latency_delta{p95,p99,tenant} (gauge)
- hosted_burst_cost_estimate{tenant,window} (gauge)
- rollback_count{reason} (counter)

Runbook (short):
- On unexpected bleed rollback spike: 1) Pause handshake globally for affected region via feature flag; 2) Inspect bleed_latency_delta and error rates; 3) If variant demotion caused quality regressions, revert to higher-quality variant or route to dedicated with backpressure; 4) Notify SRE and customer success for tenants affected.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for state transitions and timeouts.
- Integration test that simulates dedicated capacity exhaustion and verifies phased transition to hosted.
- Chaos test: inject hosted latency tail and confirm automatic rollback within SLA window.
- E2E bench: run with 10 synthetic tenants and verify cost estimates and telemetry.

Security and compliance:
- No customer data movement changes; handshake only alters route selection.
- For Private/VPC tenants we will default to Blocked unless tenant opted into hosted backfill. Add security_review_required label on config UI changes.

Migration and rollout plan:
- v1: feature flagged rollout for internal tenants only (SRE + 3 pilot customers).
- v2: enable for broader set with tenant-level controls in Console.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: noisy neighbor increases on hosted during multi-tenant bleed. Mitigation: per-tenant hosted burst budgets and global throttles.
- Risk: model quality regressions because hosted variant differs. Mitigation: probe stage and automatic regression detection using eval prompt set.
- Risk: orchestration split-brain. Mitigation: store handshake state in routing-store with versioning and leader election.

Next steps and checklist:
- [x] Finalize design doc (Maya)
- [x] Proto API sketch (Luca)
- [ ] Implement orchestrator state machine (Luca)
- [ ] Quota controller changes (Anika)
